papers.title: Natural Language Can Help Bridge the Sim2Real Gap
papers.title_zh: Natural Language Can Help Bridge the Sim2Real Gap
papers.tldr_zh: The main challenge in learning image-conditioned robotic pol
papers.cover_zh: The main challenge in learning image-conditioned robotic pol
papers.abstract_zh: The main challenge in learning image-conditioned robotic policies is acquiring a visual representation conducive to low-level control. Due to the high dimensionality of the image space, learning a good visual representation requires a considerable amount of visual data. However, when learning in the real world, data is expensive. Sim2Real is a promising paradigm for overcoming data scarcity in the real-world target domain by using a simulator to collect large amounts of cheap data closely related to the target task. However, it is difficult to transfer an image-conditioned policy from sim to real when the domains are very visually dissimilar. To bridge the sim2real visual gap, we propose using natural language descriptions of images as a unifying signal across domains that captures the underlying task-relevant semantics. Our key insight is that if two image observations from different domains are labeled with similar language, the policy should predict similar action distributions for both images. We demonstrate that training the image encoder to predict the language description or the distance between descriptions of a sim or real image serves as a useful, data-efficient pretraining step that helps learn a domain-invariant image representation. We can then use this image encoder as the backbone of an IL policy trained simultaneously on a large amount of simulated and a handful of real demonstrations. Our approach outperforms widely used prior sim2real methods and strong vision-language pretraining baselines like CLIP and R3M by 25 to 40%. See additional videos and materials at https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/lang4sim2real/.

papers.title: SEEK: Semantic Reasoning for Object Goal Navigation in Real World Inspection Tasks
papers.title_zh: SEEK：面向真实世界检测任务的物体目标导航语义推理
papers.tldr_zh: 提出SEEK框架，利用语义先验知识提升真实世界物体目标导航效率。
papers.cover_zh: 机器人也能像人类一样推理？｜新框架让检测效率碾压LLM
papers.abstract_zh: 本文解决了真实环境中自主检测的物体目标导航问题。物体目标导航对于在各种场景下实现有效检测至关重要，通常需要机器人在大搜索空间中识别目标物体。当前的物体检测方法无法达到人类效率，因为它们通常无法像人类一样利用先验知识和常识。本文提出了一种框架，使机器人能够利用来自环境先验空间配置的语义知识和语义常识。我们提出了SEEK（物体检测任务的语义推理），它将语义先验知识与机器人的观测相结合，以更高效地搜索和导航至目标物体。SEEK维护两种表示：动态场景图（DSG）和关系语义网络（RSN）。RSN是一个紧凑且实用的模型，用于估计在DSG的空间元素中找到目标物体的概率。我们提出了一种新颖的概率规划框架，利用关系语义知识搜索物体。我们的仿真分析表明，在物体目标检测任务的效率方面，SEEK优于本研究考察的经典规划和基于大语言模型（LLMs）的方法。我们在城市环境中的物理腿式机器人上验证了该方法，展示了其在真实检测场景中的实用性和有效性。
